new_note: *And when we were carried away captives to Nineve, all my brothers and those that were of my kindred did eat of the bread of the Gentiles.* (Tobit 1:10). *For one believeth that he may eat all things: another, who is weak, eateth herbs* (Romans 14:2). The weak brother who *eateth herbs* is doing in Rome what Tobit did in the captivity — refusing the meat of the heathen table, whose slaughter and offering could not be trusted. The abstaining is a conscience guarding itself from defilement by association, not a verdict that the Torah's own clean food had changed.

new_note: *When the ungodly perished, she delivered the righteous man, who fled from the fire which fell down upon the five cities.* (Wisdom of Solomon 10:6). *And, in like manner, Elohim (God) will execute judgment on the places where they have done according to the uncleanness of the Sodomites, like to the judgment of Sodom.* (Jubilees 16:6). Jubilees goes on in the next verse to tell how Lot was saved because Elohim (God) remembered Abraham and sent him out of the midst of the overthrow; Wisdom names the same deliverance from the other side — the righteous man delivered from the fire that fell on the five cities. The judgment on Sodom and the rescue of the righteous out of it are one act, told in both books.

new_note: *And the world shall be turned into the old silence seven days, like as in the former judgments: so that no man shall remain.* (2 Esdras 7:30). *I beheld the earth, and, lo, it was without form, and void; and the heavens, and they had no light.* (Jeremiah 4:23). Esdras is told the world returns to the old silence for seven days, no man remaining. Jeremiah was shown the like: the earth *without form, and void,* the heavens without light, and, as he goes on, *lo, there was no man* (Jeremiah 4:25). These are the words of the earth before the first day, when *the earth was without form, and void; and darkness was upon the face of the deep* (Genesis 1:2); the old silence is the earth returned to that first stillness, no man remaining, before *the earth shall restore those that are asleep in her* (2 Esdras 7:32).
reason: The flagged quote was Jeremiah 4:23–26 (canon side) leading the note. Reordered so 2 Esdras 7:30 stands first in italics and Jeremiah 4:23 is quoted from text_canon. Jeremiah 4:25 and Genesis 1:2 phrases are kept from the old note (not in the packet). No member rows.
